- `percent <category> <whole percent from 1 to 100>`: that percent off every line of that category,
  rounded down to whole cents.
- `fixed <sku> <amount, like 1.50>`: that amount off each unit of that product; a line never goes below 0.
- `threshold <minimum amount> <amount off>`: that amount off the whole order when the order's discounted

  that subtotal.

counts.

threshold discount applies to the order and does not change the tax.

## Cause

`price_order` priced each line on its own: `amount = line_price(product, line.quantity)`. BK-14 has a 2-for-16.20 bundle, so a single-unit line falls below `bundle_size` and pays the unit price — twice 10.70 = 21.40. The order was quoted per line, ignoring that the two lines together are 2 units.

That contradicts the documented rule in `docs/pricing.md`: "**Every unit of a product in the order counts towards its bundles.**" (This predates the discount work — `pricing.py` is unchanged in that respect since commit `ebc939c`; it only surfaced now.)

## Fix

`quotewell/pricing.py` — line totals are now computed by a new `allocate_line_totals(quantities, products)`: lines are grouped by sku, the group's units are priced together with `line_price`, and the pooled amount is split back over the group's lines in proportion to their quantities by `split_amount(cents, weights)` (integer floor shares, leftover cents one each to the largest weights, earliest first). Single-line skus and non-bundle products are unchanged, and subtotals are identical to the old per-line pricing whenever there's one line per sku — which is why the legacy quotes still hold.

The rest of the pipeline is untouched: each line still takes the larger of percent/fixed, tax is charged per line after its discount, and the threshold still comes off the order without touching tax.
